item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00170","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C12","C22","C14"],"selected_candidate_label":"C12","confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C12 is a concrete and material drafting precursor. It establishes the Mutual Security Act administrative framework, expressly reserves the President's section 507 coordination function later implemented by the child, assigns supervisory responsibility to the Director for Mutual Security, and uses several formulations carried into the child. Most notably, C12 requires the Secretary of Defense to keep the Director “fully and currently informed” of matters including “prospective action,” while the child requires representatives to keep mission chiefs and each other “fully and currently informed” of matters including “prospective plans, recommendations, and actions.” The child also substantially reproduces C12's prior-order control and continuity machinery. C22 and C14 offer narrower structural precedents concerning a chief of mission coordinating multiple United States representatives and referring disagreements upward, but neither matches the child's Mutual Security machinery as directly as C12.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The Chief of the United States Diplomatic Mission in each country ... shall coordinate the activities of the United States representatives ... engaged in carrying out programs under the Mutual Security Act of 1951.","parent_excerpt":"There are hereby excluded from the functions delegated by section 1(a) ... [t]he functions conferred upon the President by sections 502(c), 503, 507, and 530 of the said Mutual Security Act of 1951.","explanation":"C12 created the governing delegation scheme while specifically reserving the section 507 coordination authority that the child then exercised in detail."},{"child_excerpt":"The Director for Mutual Security shall be responsible for assuring the carrying out of the provisions of this order.","parent_excerpt":"The administration of programs ... shall be subject to coordination, direction, and supervision by the Director for Mutual Security.","explanation":"Both assign the Director materially similar coordinating and supervisory machinery within the same Mutual Security program."},{"child_excerpt":"shall keep the respective Chiefs of United States Diplomatic Missions and each other fully and currently informed on all matters, including prospective plans, recommendations, and actions","parent_excerpt":"The Secretary of Defense shall keep the Director for Mutual Security fully and currently informed of all matters, including prospective action","explanation":"The distinctive phrase and information-flow requirement are closely adapted from C12 to a country-level chain of coordination."},{"child_excerpt":"To the extent that provisions of any prior order are inconsistent with the provisions of this order, the latter shall control ... All orders, regulations, rulings, certificates, directives and other actions ... shall remain in effect except as they are inconsistent herewith or are hereafter amended or revoked under proper authority.","parent_excerpt":"To the extent that any provision of any prior Executive order is inconsistent with the provisions of this order, the latter shall control ... All orders, regulations, rulings, certificates, directives, agreements, contracts, delegations, and other actions ... shall remain in effect except as they are inconsistent herewith or are hereafter amended or revoked under proper authority.","explanation":"The child substantially reproduces C12's two-part prior-order control and continuity clause, with limited tailoring."}]}
